E022-01.notes: Object of 'assigned' -> 'my partner and me'; drop 'my partner and' test. 'I' sounds formal, so it is a classic trap; 'myself' has no antecedent; 'mine' is possessive.

E022-02.notes: Narrative is in past tense ('Last fall', 'was', 'wrote'); 'visited' required.

flags: minor: D ('with care and carefully') is an obviously redundant throwaway distractor

E022-05.notes: Nonrestrictive clause closed by a comma after 'down', so it must open with a matching comma; dash/comma mismatch in NO CHANGE; semicolon and no punctuation fail.

flags: minor: the passage for this item shows an empty position marker '[]' after Sentence 4 that no choice references; it is harmless but stray (possibly meant to mark the paragraph end)
E022-06.notes: 'Then we checked each batch with him' needs batches to exist first, so it follows Sentence 3 (cooking three times) and precedes Sentence 4 (the third try).

E022-07.notes: Only two Nigerian recipes are compared, so comparative 'the more popular'. 'most' (C) is still superlative; B is ungrammatical. Many quick solvers keep NO CHANGE.

E022-08.notes: Colon after a complete independent clause introducing a list. Comma makes 'four countries' read as a list item; semicolon needs an independent clause after it; no punctuation runs together.

E022-09.notes: Noun after 'The' -> 'effect'. 'affects' plural/verb conflicts with 'surprised'; 'affected' is a verb/adjective.
